title: Two ideals have the same zero locus iff they have the same radical
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an ideal $I\subset R$ let $V(I)=\{\mathfrak p\subset R\text{ prime}: I\subset\mathfrak p\}$ and $\sqrt I=\{x\in R: x^n\in I\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$. Then $\sqrt I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in V(I)}\mathfrak p$, and for ideals $I,J\subset R$ one has $V(I)=V(J)$ if and only if $\sqrt I=\sqrt J$. In particular two radical ideals ($I=\sqrt I$, $J=\sqrt J$) with $V(I)=V(J)$ are equal.
